The method replaces the standard point-sampled spectrum (uniform frequency bins) with a dynamic piecewise linear representation.
*   **Spectral Representation:** Instead of discrete bins, the spectrum is represented as a set of linear segments defined by their endpoints (wavelength $\lambda$ and intensity $I$).
**Ray Casting Setup:** For each pixel, cast a ray through the volume.
*   Calculate the Doppler shift for each wavelength component based on the relative velocity between the emitter (voxel) and the observer (camera).
*   Apply the Lambert-Bouguer law for attenuation.
*   Accumulate the spectral contributions along the ray using front-to-back alpha compositing in the spectral domain.
*   **Spectral Resolution:** The number of linear segments used to represent the spectrum.
*   **Velocity Field:** The magnitude and direction of motion.
*   **Energy Conservation:** Point-sampled methods suffer from energy conservation inaccuracies when spectral lines shift between bins.
*   **Spectral Loss:** If the bin range is not large enough, information can be lost when emission/absorption computations shift from the visible into the invisible spectrum.
*   **Spectral Broadening:** Velocities vary continuously along ray segments, causing spectral broadening.
*   **Time Complexity:** The method is more computationally expensive than standard volume rendering due to the spectral calculations and Doppler shift computations.
It builds on the work of Noordmans et al. [NvdVS00] who first introduced spectral volume rendering using point-sampled spectra.
